form_cues: Keep the left forearm comfortably supported; no pressing into the mat.
Lift with your legs and glutes; use no weight, band, or arm drive.
Stop at a comfortable straight line from shoulders to knees; do not arch the lower back.
Skip if getting down or back up requires the injured arm.
notes: Unloaded bridge, distinct from the existing dumbbell glute bridge. Left-arm support and safe floor transfers are required; this is not an arm rehabilitation exercise.
instructions: Use a mat only if you can get down and back up safely without pushing, gripping, or bearing weight through the left arm. Otherwise skip this exercise.

Lie on your back with knees bent and feet about hip-width apart. Rest the left forearm comfortably on a cushion or beside your torso without pressure through it; do not force the elbow straight or the palm upward.
Exhale gently and lift the hips using the glutes and feet. Keep both arms relaxed; do not press either hand or forearm into the mat to assist.
Pause briefly at a comfortable height without arching your lower back, then lower the hips slowly. Stop if the position or movement brings on arm symptoms.
Finish by returning your hips to the mat, then use your planned safe exit without pushing off with the left hand or elbow.
